examples.title: High sea level, October 2026
examples.text: October 2026 ran nearly a foot above normal sea level, the highest anomaly in the record, as in El Niño years. A 7.3 ft tide, 1.5 ft above the prediction, coincided with a 0.2 ft jump in the slough within an hour.

examples.title: Storm surge tops the berm, May 2026
examples.text: Spring tides ran about half a foot above the prediction. Three high tides reached up to 7.2 ft and each one stepped the slough up, adding about 0.5 ft with no rain.

examples.title: Waves at high tide, August 2025
examples.text: Ordinary tides with little surge (0.1 ft), yet the slough stepped up at each high tide, about 1.1 ft over three days with no rain. Summer swell running up the beach at high tide is the likely carrier.

examples.title: Spring tides and waves, May 2020
examples.text: Five high tides in a row stepped the slough up about 1 ft in four days, with spring tides about 0.3 ft above the prediction and no rain to speak of.
